sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美西语近岸软件研发外包与数字客服中心

business_scope.primary_industry_name: AI Video Synthesis and Virtual Avatar Generation Software

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law 526 of 1999 (UIAF and AML/CFT framework); Law 1121 of 2006 (Anti-Money Laundering obligations); Decree 830 of 2021 (UBO Registration – Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales, RUB); Resolution DIAN No. 164 of 2021 (RUB procedural rules)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport of each individual shareholder/UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of address (utility bill or bank statement) of each UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or licensed financial institution in country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or corporate extract for any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registry of Companies in jurisdiction of incorporation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized power of attorney for the incorporation agent or legal representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in country of origin or Colombian Notary

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory PEP screening against the UIAF (Unidad de Información y Análisis Financiero) official list and the Colombian Attorney General's criminal records register; sanctions screening against OFAC SDN List, UN Consolidated List, and EU Consolidated List; enhanced due diligence required for any PEP, family member, or close associate; ongoing transaction monitoring and annual certification of RUB data per DIAN Resolution 164 of 2021.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: RUES (Registro Único Empresarial y Social) – www.rue.com.co / local Cámara de Comercio (Chamber of Commerce) online portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be written in Spanish or in a language with Latin-script transliteration that preserves a phonetically identifiable Spanish pronunciation; any foreign-language name must include a Spanish translation in the articles of association; all official registry entries are recorded in the Spanish alphabet.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant may file a reconsideration petition (recurso de reposición) with the issuing Chamber of Commerce within 10 business days of notification; if reconsideration is denied, the applicant may appeal to the Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio within 20 business days; the applicant may renew the clearance request after 30 days with a different name token set.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office permitted for the registered address, provided it consists of a physical geolocatable address within Colombian territory, designated for service of process and official notices, and is not a P.O. Box; serviced offices and coworking spaces with a physical reception desk are acceptable for low-risk SaaS operations.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low – approximately 15% within the first year of operation; no mandatory scheduled inspection for ISIC 6201; unannounced visits may occur if inconsistent data are flagged by the UIAF or DIAN.

Notarization of private incorporation instrument and corporate bylaws

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registration with Chamber of Commerce and RUES
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory registration fee (staggered small company scale)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory platform fee and market benchmark for compliance services

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Miscellaneous administrative charges – digital certificates, copies, courier, and incidental registry expenses

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 1258 de 2008 (Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada), Arts. 1-12, 18, 22; Código de Comercio, Arts. 110-125 (registration of commercial entities).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cámara de Comercio del domicilio social (Superintendencia de Sociedades exercises residual supervisory jurisdiction).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Documento privado de constitución, radicado ante la Cámara de Comercio for commercial registry inscription.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No legal minimum capital for S.A.S.; capital is freely fixed by the incorporators. No escrow account or judicial deposit requirement exists under Colombian corporate law.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) The share subscriptions and capital contributions set out in the subscribed capital schedule are approved and accepted. (2) The registered office of the Company is fixed at the address stated in the bylaws, subject to future relocation by the legal representative. (3) [Name] and [Name] are appointed as Manager and Deputy Manager, with all powers conferred by the S.A.S. regulations and the Company's bylaws. (4) The legal representative is empowered to execute all filings before the Commercial Registry, tax authorities, and other governmental offices, and to take all actions necessary to commence lawful operations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare and execute the private incorporation document
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary and the appointed shareholders; subsequent registration with Cámara de Comercio
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the private incorporation document (Documento Privado de Constitución) containing the company name, domicile, purpose, capital subscriptions, management structure, and internal governance rules. The document must be signed by the founding shareholders. If assets other than cash are contributed, a verbal or written description and valuation methodology must be attached and approved. Notarization is optional unless real property is contributed.
required_dossiers: Private incorporation document signed by shareholders
Identification documents (ID, passport, or NIT) of each shareholder
Subscribed and paid capital schedule
RUV (Registro Único Tributario) pre-registration data, if available
Proof of legal representative acceptance (fiducia, consent form)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Chamber of Commerce returns the filing for omissions, correct the deficiencies in the private document and resubmit the entire application within the same registry process without payment of a new filing fee unless a substantive change is introduced.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submit the incorporation document to the Commercial Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio (local chamber corresponding to registered domicile)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the signed private incorporation document and supporting annexes through the Chamber's online portal (SIRI - Sistema de Información Registral) or in person at the delegated branch. Request simultaneous issuance of the Certificate of Existence and Representation (Certificado de Existencia y Representación) and assignment of the NIT (rush process). Pay the applicable registration and certificate fees via the Chamber's payment gateway.
required_dossiers: Private incorporation document
Shareholder identification and valid authorizations
RUE (Registro Único Empresarial) form (electronic)
Proof of payment of registration fees
Form used to apply for NIT (if not already issued)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a 'preventive measure' (anotación, cancelation, or corrective requirement), remedy the specific observation within 10 business days by submitting corrected documents or clarifications to the same registry officer; a formal appeal (recurso de reposición y apelación) is available against final adverse decisions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain the Tax ID (RUT) and enroll in the national tax administration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the RUT (Registro Único Tributario) electronic enrollment via the DIAN website using the NIT assigned by the Chamber. Indicate the applicable tax regime (generally the ordinary regime for companies), income tax, VAT (IVA), and withholding agent obligations, as applicable. Upon completion, the software will confirm the company's RUT and authorize generation of electronic invoices.
required_dossiers: Certificado de Existencia y Representación issued by the Chamber
Legal representative identification
Company activity code (ISIC 6201)
Bank account information (if withholding agent designations apply)
Digital certificate / electronic signature (firma electrónica)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RUT application is delayed or denied, file an 'aclaración de RUT' online with correct documents; administrative appeals follow DIAN's Dispute Resolution Chapter. The legal representative may also request urgent attention through the DIAN call center.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register the company with the social security and occupational risk system
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Welfare funds (cajas de compensación) and Risk Administrators (ARL)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company as a contributor (empleador) with the applicable social security entity (EPS, pension fund, and ARL) for its employees. For a remote software development company, the required ARL affiliation is based on the professional risk class; register the employees once the NIT and RUT are active. This step is mandatory before hiring any personnel or initiating payroll.
required_dossiers: RUT
Certificado de Existencia y Representación
Legal representative identification
Bank account details for payroll contributions
List of initial employees and their information
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the ARL or welfare fund rejects registration, correct the classification (use activity code 6201) and resubmit; if rejection persists, request a revised risk rating from the Ministry of Labor's regional office.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for ISIC 6201; the activity does not require industrial manufacturing licensing. However, the Ministry of Information Technologies and Communications (MinTIC) may regulate online data processing services, and the SIC (Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio) oversees data protection compliance.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable; no operating license is required for pure software development and AI video generation services that have no physical manufacturing facility.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – No EIA required. Office-based / software development activities are outside ANLA licensing thresholds.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater, air emission, or hazardous waste streams are generated. If the company later hosts servers, compliance with Colombian network operators' regulations and power consumption standards for data centers must be verified, but no environmental license is required.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety inspection and structural load certification are required only for physical premises. For an office environment, the company must obtain the certificate of building safety from the relevant municipal fire department (Bomberos) and ensure workplace ergonomics and hygiene per Resolution 2400 of 1979. Because the primary operations are remote software development, staff must also complete occupational risk prevention training under the ARL.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN); official portal www.dian.gov.co and transactional platform MUISCA
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign sponsor incorporates the S.A.S. before a notary and registers the deed with the Chamber of Commerce (Cámara de Comercio). The company must then register in the Registro Único Tributario (RUT) via DIAN's MUISCA portal (Formulario Pre-RUT) to obtain the Número de Identificación Tributaria (NIT). The S.A.S. must designate a legal representative resident in Colombia for tax compliance; foreign shareholders without Colombian presence are subject to local withholding tax on distributions, requiring the entity to enroll in withholding-regime categories. A foreign vendor providing or receiving services in Colombia should also obtain a NIT for tax-payer identification when generating Colombian-source income, but a local permanent establishment triggers full RUT registration obligations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: An S.A.S. incorporated under Colombian law is a Colombian tax resident taxed on worldwide income (corporate income tax, CIT) at 35% for tax year 2024, falling to 30% from tax year 2025. No pass-through election is permitted. Non-residents are taxed only on Colombian-source income.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch election exists; Colombia applies mandatory anti-hybrid rules under Law 1819/2016 (aligned with BEPS Action 2). Optional elective regimes include: (i) ZESE – Zona Económica y Social Especial, a reduced CIT rate (26% for the first 5 years) for new companies established in qualifying municipalities; (ii) creative-industries (Orange Economy) tax incentive potentially available to new software/content-development ventures meeting Decree-979/2020 conditions; (iii) exemption of certain custom software fabrication services from VAT where applicable.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: IVA – Impuesto sobre las Ventas (Value Added Tax)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No turnover threshold applies to commercial companies: every S.A.S. engaged in taxable operations must obtain a NIT and register in the RUT in the Régimen Común, regardless of sales volume. The simplified VAT regime (for sole proprietors with gross income under 3,500 UVT, approx. COP 125 million) is unavailable to S.A.S. entities.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic invoicing (factura electrónica) with pre-issuance real-time validation by DIAN. Invoices must be generated through a DIAN-authorized technology provider (proveedor tecnológico) or DIAN's free billing tool, in the authorized XML schema (CUFE/CUDE with UUID and QR code), and submitted to DIAN's Hab.Se web services (FE-V1) for prior validation. Electronic issuance is obligatory for exports of services and for filing VAT-refund requests.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of services, including AI video synthesis and virtual-avatar SaaS, qualify for a 0% VAT rate (exempt with right to refund) under Article 481(e) of the Tax Statute and Decree 2248/2014 where: (i) the service is provided from Colombia to a foreign beneficiary without domicile in Colombia; (ii) the service is used exclusively abroad; and (iii) the contract is evidenced in writing and no local real estate or Colombian territorial exploitation is involved. Revenue must be ingressed through the foreign-exchange market.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Signed export-services contract (bilingual or officially translated to Spanish) demonstrating exclusive foreign use
DIAN-validated electronic commercial invoice (factura electrónica) referencing the contract
Formulario de Declaración de Cambio No. 4 (foreign-exchange settlement certificate) issued by an authorized Colombian bank or FX intermediary
Proof of inbound remittance (SWIFT confirmation, Stripe/Paddle payout statement) evidencing receipt of export proceeds
RUT certificate showing IVA registration and export-service activity status
Certificate of existence and legal representation for the S.A.S. (Cámara de Comercio) if required by DIAN on audit
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DIAN scrutinizes export-refund claims on substantial and documentary grounds; improper refunds are clawed back with daily arrears interest computed from the original refund payment (Article 118 ET) plus an additional penalty of up to 100% of the amount evaded (Article 647(1) ET) and a 4% monthly-equivalent late-interest adjustment. False or fraudulent export zero-rating claims to obtain VAT refunds constitute criminal tax evasion under Law 1943/2018, Articles 102 ff., carrying imprisonment of up to 9 years and fines of multiples of the defrauded amount. Failure to repatriate export proceeds within 180 days may trigger exchange-infringement penalties under Banco de la República rules and disqualification from the zero-rate treatment.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de la República de Colombia (the Central Bank of Colombia), acting through its governing board, the Junta Directiva del Banco de la República; the national foreign-exchange framework comprises Law 9 of 1991, Resolution 8 of 2000 (as amended), Decree 1368 of 2021 and prudential rules issued by the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia; only authorized commercial banks enrolled in the Mercado Cambiario may lawfully act as exchange intermediaries; the DIAN (Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales) enforces exchange-control penalties and customs-related FX duties.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Colombia operates a market-based free-convertibility regime for current-account items: software-export revenues, AI-content royalties and international service fees are freely receivable and convertible at the free-market TRM through authorized intermediaries without prior Central Bank approval. Capital-account flows, including paid-in equity from the non-resident shareholder, are also permissible but require mandatory ex-post registration with Banco de la República in the foreign-investment registry; that registration alone confers the legal entitlement to remit future dividends/profits and to repatriate invested capital. Dividend-profit remittance is not capped or deferred, but the two gateways are: (i) valid registration of the foreign investment, and (ii) prior payment of the Colombian dividend withholding tax together with certification by the Revisor Fiscal or independent accountant that the distributable profits exist in the audited books. The practical hurdles are documentary and administrative, not substantive: late or defective investment registration temporarily suspends remittance rights and attracts exchange-control fines, whereas current-account convertibility remains unrestricted.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under Decree 1368 of 2021 and Resolution 8 of 2000, the exporter must channel 100% of services-export proceeds — including AIGC SaaS subscription fees received via Stripe/Paddle aggregations — into the Colombian Mercado Cambiario through an authorized commercial bank within 6 months from the date of the export (for services; computed from invoicing/performance); goods-export proceeds enjoy the same 6-month term, extendable by up to 4 additional months. There is no fixed monetary surrender ratio payable to the Central Bank; the obligation is the full-channeling duty, meaning the entire export value must enter the national banking system either as conversion to COP at the free TRM or as a credit to the exporter's foreign-currency deposit account at an authorized local intermediary. Offshore retention of export proceeds without a prior 'administración de divisas' authorization is prohibited; breach triggers DIAN exchange-control penalties and loss of export-incentive privileges. For the digital-service exporter, the critical operational risk is aggregation: each monthly payout from Stripe/Paddle must be traceable to individual software-export invoices so the bank can file the corresponding exchange declaration.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Rating: LOW-to-MEDIUM legal viability as a primary treasury rail. Offshore digital EMIs (Wise, Deel, Payoneer, Mercury, Brex) are not authorized Colombian exchange-market participants and cannot lawfully receive or settle the SAS's software-export proceeds; using them as the principal collection account would breach the 6-month channeling duty, trigger exchange-control fines and undermine bankability at the Tier-1 institution. EMIs remain legally usable for ancillary operational outflows (e.g., low-value international contractor payments) provided the outflows are documented and, when required, reflected in the periodic FX information filed through the authorized intermediary. Onshore fintechs with a local banking license (Lulo Bank; Nequi, supervised by the Superintendencia Financiera) are viable only as supporting expense/operational accounts, not as the statutory FX-channeling vehicle. Recommended architecture: one Tier-1 commercial bank account as the single forex-channeling backbone; Stripe/Paddle consolidated payouts remitted monthly into that account; offshore EMIs confined to foreign micro-payments and expressly disclosed in the treasury compliance file.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Complete remote opening for a newly formed S.A.S. with foreign control is not available in practice. The designated legal representative or a locally appointed attorney-in-fact must be identified in person at the bank branch for final signature and biometric capture; non-resident directors may execute, before a Colombian consulate abroad, an apostilled special power of attorney (poder especial) authorizing a Colombian-resident abogado or general manager to open and operate the account, but the bank will still mandate a live video-KYC interview with the ultimate beneficial owner and, commonly, an in-person branch visit by the attorney-in-fact. Physical verification of the corporate address (lease contract or registered virtual office) and a certified Cámara de Comercio extract issued within 30 days are mandatory onboarding items; the RUT and incorporation deed must be presented in certified/apostilled form. Plan a 2–6 week onboarding calendar including consular legalization cycles; documents-by-email-only onboarding is unavailable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Shell-company red flag: newly registered S.A.S. with a single non-resident shareholder, no local payroll, no operating history and minimal initial capital at bank's first cut-off.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled incorporation deed and shareholders' register evidencing the full UBO chain; accountant-issued opening balance sheet; 12-month bank statements and a source-of-funds letter from the shareholder; executed SaaS customer contracts and Stripe/Paddle revenue summaries proving recurrent B2B receipts; Colombian RUT and Cámara de Comercio certificate; evidence of local substance (office lease, developer employment agreements or local payroll); completed SARLAFT risk questionnaire signed by the UBO.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO jurisdiction/address mismatch: UBO passport and tax residency in an elevated-opacity jurisdiction, or divergence between the corporate registered seat and UBO residence, causing inconsistent addresses in the bank's name-screening engines.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Structured UBO declaration on the SARLAFT-certified form; apostilled passport copy; certified proof of residential address; group-structure memorandum explaining ownership rationale; corroboration of UBO professional history and absence of PEP status; the UBO's own bank reference letter from a reputable foreign institution; declaration of absence of sanctioned-country nexus.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: AI/video-generation business-scope flag: 'AI Avatar and Synthetic Video Generation Software' raises bank alerts for potential deepfake fraud, identity-related misuse or virtual-asset-adjacent reputational risk, particularly if customer traffic is anonymous.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Compliance dossier containing the platform's content-use policy prohibiting unauthorized manipulation of identifiable persons; SIC data-protection registration under Law 1581 of 2012; privacy/DPA terms governing end customers; KYC/merchant screening measures applied through Stripe/Paddle; AI-watermarking and provenance-standard disclosures; executed enterprise sales contracts demonstrating legitimate commercial channels; AML officer confirmation of the 'Low_Risk_Standard' classification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity aggregated USD inflows: dozens or hundreds of low-ticket subscription payments aggregated by Stripe/Paddle trigger the bank's transaction-laundering and structuring detection when the ledger lacks per-customer invoice correspondence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Standing treasury protocol with monthly reconciliation of Stripe/Paddle payout summaries against declared export invoices; submission of the raw merchant settlement reports to the bank for FX-declaration support; accountant certification that every aggregated credit corresponds to a software-export subscription sale; signed declaration that no third-party pass-through or personal-account flows exist; annual Revisor Fiscal certification that export proceeds are channeled exclusively through the authorized intermediary account.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant sequence for the non-resident shareholder's USD equity injection: (1) the offshore bank remits via SWIFT MT103 (or MT202/MT202COV where same-day cover is required); Field 50K must show the remitter exactly as registered, Field 59 the S.A.S. as beneficiary, and Field 70 must carry ISO 20022 External Purpose Code 'INTC' (intra-company payment) with the narrative 'EQUITY CONTRIBUTION / CAPITAL INCREASE — COLOMBIAN S.A.S.'; (2) the receiving Tier-1 bank, as authorized exchange intermediary, applies SARLAFT screening to confirm that the remitter is the actual registered shareholder; (3) the funds are credited to a COP account (converted at the TRM) or to a USD foreign-currency account of the SAS, and the bank simultaneously files the exchange declaration with Banco de la República; (4) the legal representative completes the Banco de la República foreign-investment registration (inversión internacional directa), which serves as the legal title for future dividend remittances and capital repatriation; (5) corporate formalities are archived, including the shareholders' approval minute, the Cámara de Comercio capital annotation, the RUT update and the banker's capital certificate. Routing through EMIs, crypto exchanges or personal accounts is prohibited for FDI recognition.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing-rail matrix: (a) SWIFT MT103 (with ISO purpose codes such as 'TRAD' or 'INTC' for intra-group cross-border cost payments) is the default rail for trade disbursements, covering GPU-cloud providers, CDN licensing, foreign legal/tax advisors and international contractor payments; outflows are declared in the exchange regime when they exceed the bank's reporting threshold (generally USD 10,000-equivalent per operation or lower per policy); (b) MT202/MT202COV supports interbank funding of the company's offshore EMI accounts, subject to upstream underlying-expense documentation; (c) Commercial and Standby Letters of Credit are available for high-value OEM/distribution or infrastructure procurement: when the S.A.S. is exporter/beneficiary, the LC guarantees payment against presentation of software acceptance certificates or milestone invoices; when the S.A.S. imports GPU capacity for its AI rendering pipeline, a documentary LC mitigates counterparty risk; (d) domestic COP flows (payroll, rent, utilities, DIAN taxes) run on the local PSE/ACH clearing network, while Stripe and Paddle consolidated payouts are received into the same Tier-1 account and channeled against the corresponding export declarations. Every settlement architecture must preserve invoice-tagging discipline so that each MT103 carries the contractual reference recoverable by the bank's compliance function.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright COP/USD forward contracts (forwards) traded with an authorized Colombian exchange intermediary, with delivery at the TRM, for hedging forecast USD export receivables
Non-deliverable COP/USD forwards (NDFs) settled in COP against the TRM reference rate, usable where a real USD exposure is forecast but physical delivery is not desired
COP/USD cross-currency swaps covering principal and coupon flows, permissible when the SAS holds a matching USD liability, e.g., international financing for GPU-capacity capital expenditure
European-style COP/USD FX options purchased from onshore bank trading desks as premium-based protection against adverse TRM movements on large-ticket licensing receipts

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Mercantile Registry Renewal (Renovación de la Matrícula Mercantil)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By March 31 of each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal triggers a surcharge of 10% of the registry fee for each month of delay (capped at 12 months), eventual cancellation of the mercantile registration, loss of access to official certificates, and inadmissibility in commercial transactions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Approved Financial Statements Registration (Aprobación y Registro de Estados Financieros)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Ordinary shareholders' meeting no later than March 31; registration within one month following approval (generally by April 30)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance may block corporate transactions, prevent legal distribution of dividends, and trigger fines of up to 400 current monthly minimum wages (SMMLV) imposed by the Superintendencia de Sociedades; continued default may lead to dissolution or regulatory enforcement.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Owners Report (Reporte de Beneficiarios Finales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DIAN (Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: June 1 to June 30 of each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or omitted filing may incur fines up to 10,000 UVT under official tax regulations; repeated violations can lead to additional penalties against directors, legal representatives, and tax responsibility assessments.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return and Complementary Declarations (Declaración de Renta y Complementarios)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DIAN (Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filing window based on NIT last digit, generally between April and June of the following fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing imposes a fine of up to 5% of the tax assessed, plus default interest; outright failure to file or fraudulent reporting subjects the entity to fines up to 10,000 UVT, tax account freezing, and potentially criminal liability for the legal representative.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A mandatory statutory auditor (Revisor Fiscal) is required for a Colombian SAS if (i) total assets exceed 5,000 SMMLV, (ii) gross operating revenues exceed 3,000 SMMLV, or (iii) the entity has more than 50 employees; additionally, mandatory audit applies when the SAS is a controlling company or is required by express legal provision.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as issued by the IASB, applicable in Colombia under Law 1314 of 2009 and Decree 2420 of 2015. Full IFRS applies to entities with significant public interest; IFRS for SMEs applies to smaller and medium-sized private SAS entities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: For any shareholding transfer occurring during the fiscal year, the SAS must update the Register of Members and submit an annual confirmation through DIAN's Beneficiarios Finales reporting system by June 30. The report must identify each direct or indirect ultimate beneficiary holding more than 5% of shares or voting rights, including full legal name, TAX ID, country of residence, type and percentage of ownership, and the chain of ownership ending at the final beneficiary.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro de Registro de Accionistas)
Register of Directors (Libro de Registro de Junta Directiva)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$180–US$600 per year for typical registered office and corporate agent services in Bogotá
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$2,500–US$8,500 per year for a certified independent audit of a small-to-mid-size AI software SaaS company

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 35% (Colombian corporate income tax – Impuesto sobre la Renta y Complementarios).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general CIT holiday for AI/video-SaaS entities. Preferential treatment is limited to (i) qualifying certified investments in science, technology and innovation deductible under Article 158-1 E.T., and (ii) the possibly expired/narrow ‘orange economy’ income-tax exemption for certified new national software projects; specific rulings are required. 2025 UVT-based NOL offset cap: the amount deducted annually cannot exceed 25% of ordinary taxable income.
